item.content:encoded:
Since they are still metallic, I'm imagining that swarm must have sounded something like a slot machine paying out.
Which is an unsettlingly upbeat soundtrack when picturing a man being nibbled to death.

And it also makes me wonder, what if they are smart enough to seek out regular coins as camouflage?
A massive population of these could be hidden away in the slots of Vegas with no one the wiser. A tourist goes to collect his winnings and…"Ouch! Must have cut myself on the edge of the machine, oh well, still won $7.50!" Most feedings wouldn't even be reported to casino staff.
And if some tourist gets drawn into a disused hallway by the glint and rattle of a "dropped" sack of coins, who's going to notice one more unexplained murder in a town with such a mob-rich history? That's if the hotel staff don't just make the corpse disappear like a dead hooker in a senator's suite to avoid bad press.
A single specimen grew to a swarm based only on what fell behind a shelf in a modest cafeteria. Imagine what could come from the leavings of a city with the largest collection of all-you-can-eat buffets on Earth.

item.title: Random Article Review #3, 7 October 2016
item.content:encoded:
Factors behind my downvote on this one:

  • The idea of a George Washington face on a quarter biting someone is far too goofy for me to go along with it on the mainlist.
  • Lapses in tone like the use of the word "remarkably" (though it's kind of funny to consider what that term means in the context of the Foundation) and using quoted terms like "mouth" and "alive" as though that's the same as a scientific term that means something.
  • The addendum is era-standard lolFoundation that portrays an incompetent organization, something I've always had problems with.

Those objections considered, this isn't a terrible example of a Series I entry. There's an internal logic to it that rises above "thing what does a thing" status, and for those that enjoy such things, it is kind of funny to imagine, I guess.

An interesting aspect of this is the addendum, which I don't like, but serves as a window into older ideas of what the Foundation was like. Site-19, where you would have to worry about horrifying monsters breaking loose and murdering you on a daily basis, but you would also have to watch out for things like your pocket change biting you. It's a more subtle reflection of the wacky madness that characterized some of the earlier visions of the Foundation, and for that it actually kind of achieves a certain charm to it that the more obnoxious, in-your-face examples of that madness never really had.
